title: —But there are many eminent French critics, said the priest, who consider that even Victor Hugo, great as he certainly was, had not so pure a French style as Louis Veuillot
html_source:
Victor Hugo was a French writer, best known for Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

“Louis Veuillot was a French journalist and author”, who supported Ultramontanism, which essentially refers great power to the papacy. It’s easy to see why the priest likes Veuillot considering this profound advocation for the papacy.
